20:1.sourceText: Ὁμοία γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ, ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.
20:1.targetText: “For the kingdom of the heavens is like to a man, a householder, who went forth with the morning to hire workmen for his vineyard,

groups.note: The actual ἅμα with the early-morning time word supplies with the morning, a temporal together-with-at-dawn expression rather than an invented accompaniment event.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with his vineyard.

20:2.sourceText: συμφωνήσας δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐργατῶν ἐκ δηναρίου τὴν ἡμέραν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ.
20:2.targetText: and having agreed with the workmen for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

groups.note: The actual accusative definite day phrase gives the agreed daily rate, rendered a day. Its Greek article and day remain together rather than claiming an independently printed indefinite article.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with his vineyard.

20:4.targetText: and to these he said, Go—also you—to the vineyard, and whatever may be righteous I will give you;

20:5.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἀπῆλθον. πάλιν δὲ ἐξελθὼν περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐνάτην ὥραν ἐποίησεν ὡσαύτως.
20:5.targetText: and they went away. Again, having gone forth about the sixth and the ninth hour, he did in like manner.

unmappedSource.reason: The second Greek δέ connective is not separately expressed after Again in this English sentence.

20:6.sourceText: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ἐξελθὼν εὗρεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί ὧδε ἑστήκατε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί;
20:6.targetText: And about the eleventh hour, having gone forth, he found others standing idle and says to them, Why have you stood here idle all day?

groups.note: The actual substantival eleventh ordinal, with the article, designates the eleventh hour by temporal ellipsis. English supplies the time-unit hour within that ordinal expression; there is no separate written Greek hour noun here.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with all day.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes idle as an earlier narrative description after standing; pinned N1904 has standing without that first idle adjective, and the actual idle address is retained at the final question.

20:7.sourceText: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο. λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα.

20:8.targetText: And evening having come, the lord of the vineyard says to his steward, Call the workmen, and pay them the reward, having begun from the last—to the first.

groups.note: The actual workmen are the commanded calling object and the same immediate recipients of the coordinated pay-the-reward command. groups.note: The actual ἀδικῶ is the do-wrong/unjust predicate, rendered I do unrighteousness. English unrighteousness belongs to that real verb, not an independently printed ἀδικία noun.

20:14.sourceText: ἆρον τὸ σὸν καὶ ὕπαγε· θέλω δὲ τούτῳ τῷ ἐσχάτῳ δοῦναι ὡς καὶ σοί·
